b: I always see this point brought up whenever someone mentions quitting YouTube or feeling down because low views and I just don’t think it’s true at all. Now it is true that you should make content you do enjoy making because it leads to better quality and a lower chance of burnout, but a lot of small YouTubers who mostly just makes let’s plays or vlogs or other content like this don’t realize how demoralizing low views can be after an extended period of time.

If you enjoy making video essays, you might still be putting in hours upon hours just to get a single 10 minute video out. The research, writing, voice over, editing, thumbnail, etc… it’s not a quick process. The sentiment that “you should be doing YouTube solely for fun” is what you should say to a 12 year old recording Fortnite gameplay. It is perfectly reasonable to start a YouTube channel with the goal of monetization, and a lot of times it should be the goal. If you’re an adult with a full time job, maybe a family too, and you have limited time and you start up a YouTube channel where you put a lot of time and effort in, you can enjoy the video making process while still pushing through the growing pains of a channel for than goal of some revenue.

I’ve been making videos for a long time and I do enjoy it, but I’m an adult with responsibilities and a job, it wouldn’t be worth it without monetization. The point of this post is to say don’t judge someone because your idea of making a YouTube channel is just to make videos for fun and have ad revenue as a nice bonus. This is a career or a potential career for a lot of people.
